title: Morning Robotics Scan
report:
## SANDO UAV Safety Planner

### The Breakthrough
MIT introduced SANDO, a trajectory planner that builds spatiotemporal safety corridors around moving obstacles using their maximum speed bounds. By surrounding each obstacle with a predictive sphere and employing a heat‑map planner, SANDO can replan on‑board in real time and provably guarantee collision‑free paths. In simulation and twelve real‑world UAV flights it reached goals faster than several prior planners with zero collisions.

### The Caveats
The superiority claim lacks concrete baseline methods or standard benchmark comparisons.

## JengaBot Pez Dispenser

### The Breakthrough
A follow‑up to the JengaBot project adds a compact, spring‑loaded Pez‑style mechanism that a robot arm can grasp and actuate to dispense single items. The design emphasizes simplicity and repeatable release for handling small objects such as candy. The demo shows the dispenser working end‑to‑end with a robot manipulator.

### The Caveats
No systematic evaluation, metrics, or quantitative evidence of effectiveness are provided beyond the informal demo.

## NeuDecide Voice‑First Model

### The Breakthrough
NeuDecide is a 43 MB end‑to‑end model that converts spoken commands directly into JSON tool calls without an intermediate transcript, running on a single CPU thread via ONNX Runtime. It combines a streaming speech encoder with a compact tool‑calling encoder‑decoder and outperforms five ASR‑plus‑decision cascades on the SLURP benchmark, achieving over five‑times higher exact‑match accuracy for 10‑tool selection. The model processes up to 30 seconds of audio with under 175 MB RAM.

### The Caveats
Its suitability for household robots is unproven, as it has never been tested on actual robot hardware and real‑world latency on embedded platforms is not reported.

## OpenHarness Agent Hub

### The Breakthrough
OpenHarness is an open‑source native app that runs multiple LLM‑based coding agents side‑by‑side, multiplexing each into its own tmux pane and streaming terminals over end‑to‑end encrypted WebRTC or relay links. It achieves sub‑15 ms UI latency on an M2 Max while using only ~0.1 % CPU and 304 MiB RAM, providing a lightweight command center for tasks ranging from CAD to robotics.

### The Caveats
Performance claims are not benchmarked against existing remote‑terminal or agent‑orchestration solutions, leaving the advantage unverified.

## Torch‑TensorRT Compiler

### The Breakthrough
Torch‑TensorRT is an open‑source compiler that converts PyTorch, TorchScript, or FX models into TensorRT engines, enabling up to 5× lower inference latency with a single line of code. It integrates with torch.compile and leverages TensorRT optimizations such as FP8 quantization and dynamic shape handling, accelerating diffusion models, Stable Diffusion, and LLMs on NVIDIA GPUs including Jetson.

### The Caveats
Speedup figures are only compared to eager PyTorch without formal evaluation or comparison to other TensorRT or optimization baselines.

## awesome‑isaac‑gym Resource List

### The Breakthrough
The awesome‑isaac‑gym repository curates 799+ links to frameworks, papers, tutorials, and tools around NVIDIA’s GPU‑accelerated Isaac Gym simulator, organized by releases, guides, research areas, and community projects. By structuring these resources in searchable markdown, it lowers the entry barrier for researchers building reinforcement‑learning or robot‑learning pipelines on Isaac Gym.

### The Caveats
The list provides no systematic evidence of completeness or up‑to‑date coverage.

### Priority
Start with SANDO because its formally verified, real‑world UAV safety guarantees directly advance autonomous navigation and present a ready‑to‑deploy solution.

### One action
Check the MIT project page and consider reproducing the safety corridor planner on your own UAV platform.
